title.value: CADet: Fully Self-Supervised Anomaly Detection With Contrastive Learning
title.justification: The title of the paper is "CADet: Fully Self-Supervised Anomaly Detection With Contrastive Learning".
title.quote: CADet: Fully Self-Supervised Anomaly Detection With Contrastive Learning

extractions.description: This paper introduces CADet, a novel self-supervised method for out-of-distribution detection of single samples. It leverages contrastive learning to detect both unseen classes and adversarial perturbations, outperforming existing adversarial detection methods and achieving comparable performance to unseen label detection methods.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper is about anomaly detection in machine learning, not directly focused on sustainable development, although it could be applied to various fields including those related to sustainability.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Handling out-of-distribution (OOD) samples has become a major stake in the real-world deployment of machine learning systems. This work explores the use of self-supervised contrastive learning to the simultaneous detection of two types of OOD samples: unseen classes and adversarial perturbations

primary_category.justification: The paper is primarily focused on machine learning techniques for anomaly detection and does not directly address any specific climate or ecologically-related sustainable development category.
primary_category.quote: We introduce CADet (Contrastive Anomaly Detection), which is able to detect OOD samples from single inputs and performs well on both label-based and adversarial detection benchmarks, without requiring access to any OOD samples to train or tune the method.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper's focus is on improving anomaly detection methods, which is a general machine learning problem. It does not focus on any specific subcategory related to Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development.
primary_sub_category.quote: We propose a novel improvement to MMD and show it can also be used to confidently detect distributional shifts when given a small number of samples.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper does not introduce a new primary category.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not introduce a new primary sub category.
